cur:monumental-san-teodoro-apse.summary: In the small round church at the foot of the Palatine, a bearded Christ in a dark robe with golden stripes sits on a blue orb, his right hand raised, flanked by Saints Peter and Paul, who in turn present Saint Theodore and another saint. The composition echoes the great apse of nearby Santi Cosma e Damiano. Christ's robe with the clavi of a high Roman official makes him the ruler of heaven and earth.
facts: The apse mosaic dates to the 6th century and shows Christ in a black robe with gold clavi, which marked high rank on Roman garments, seated on an orb.
Since 2004 the church has been used by the Greek Orthodox community of Rome, by grant of Pope John Paul II to the Ecumenical Patriarchate.

cur:monumental-san-teodoro-apse.notes: The mosaic has been restored more than once; the Commons description gives '6th and 14th cent.'

Q116242995.summary: On this small bronze reliquary cross, inlaid with niello, the crucified Christ wears a long colobium, his feet resting on a large footrest and his head inclined slightly to one side in death. On the reverse the Virgin appears with a medallion of the Christ Child before her body, an image that stresses his divinity. Worn on the breast and opening to hold a relic, such crosses joined personal devotion to the mystery of the Passion.
facts: The Met calls it a more refined example of the reliquary crosses common in the Middle Byzantine period.
Greek inscriptions give the initials of Jesus Christ on the front and of the Mother of God on the back.
It was sold by Andronicos in Constantinople in 1925 and acquired through the Brummer Gallery by the Met in 1926.
